edge_explainer: NRG fell 15.5% to a new 52-week low on a Q2 print whose headline numbers were fine (adj EBITDA $1,217M vs $909M, FY guide reaffirmed) - because the hyperscaler datacenter deal was disclosed as still only at 'principal commercial terms', unsigned. Every seed number verified from primaries EXCEPT two. First, the 'Texas weakness was ~half weather' framing is REFUTED for Q2: the 10-Q weather table shows Texas Q2-26 cooling degree days at 1,073 vs a 10-year normal of 1,035, i.e. 3.7% ABOVE normal, so there is no weather add-back; the company's own gross-margin bridge attributes the decline to a 13% ($101M) rise in cost to serve plus customer ATTRITION, and business metrics confirm average Texas Home customers -4.0% YoY and residential volume -7.1%. That is competitive repricing of ERCOT retail, not a hedging blip - and Note 6 refutes the hedging story directly, since net notional power collapsed from 103M to 34M MWh post-LS Power (NRG is LESS short generation, not more) while Q2 carried a +$289M unrealized MTM GAIN. Second, the '$3.2B fronted capex' figure appears nowhere in the 10-Q or release (the only $3.2B is the acquired LS Power debt principal) - do not carry it. Facts the seed missed: NRG DILUTED 10.5% this year (190.4M -> 210.3M shares; 24.25M issued to LS Power at $153.72), the 2026 buyback is 93% spent ($932M of a $1.0B plan through Jul-31, ~$68M left), and July revealed the priority - $980M to revolver paydown vs $14M of buybacks. Cash is $162M. THE VALUATION: NRG's current EBITDA contains essentially zero datacenter revenue, so the AI premium is entirely in the MULTIPLE. Three independent no-narrative routes converge - segment SOTP anchored on ADT at 4.98x EV/TTM-EBITDA (which cut the Vivint mark to 6.0x and removed ~$16/sh) gives $45; EV/EBITDA reversion to 6.5-7.5x gives $43-84; growth-inclusive true-FCF yield vs NRG's own tape history (16.7% in 2023, 10.3% in 2024, 8.2% today) gives $57-93. No-narrative fair value ~$68, band $55-85, leaving 27-53% of the $117 price as narrative premium. The guide itself is the second problem: it requires 2H EBITDA +59.7% YoY after a 1H that delivered +12.9%, with $300-500M of organic 2H improvement unexplained by LS Power, and NRG's own marketed '14%+ EPS growth' target needs the TOP of the 2026 range just to be met. WHAT IS REAL: NRG's own 8-K (2026-07-15) discloses 6,839 MW cleared in PJM at $325/MW-day for DY2028/29 = $811M/yr of contracted capacity revenue, and FERC extended the price COLLAR (cap ~$325-333, floor ~$175) through DY2029/30 - a genuine 3-4 year regulatory floor worth ~$550M/yr of EBITDA net of fixed O&M, indifferent to AI. Leverage (4.17x, 4.63x if 10% light) is a capital-return risk, not a solvency risk: no refi cliff before 2031 ($4,877M due through 2030 vs $2.8-3.3B/yr FCFbG). MECHANISM (the encoded knowledge): the FERC collar MASKS the AI cycle in both directions - capacity revenue cannot rise above the cap or fall below the floor for 3-4 years - so NRG's fundamentals will look AI-immune while the equity is not. The SIGNAL channel is the multiple and the unsigned contract pipeline; signal-to-price latency is ~0 for the multiple but 2-4 years for the capacity cash flows. That latency gap is exactly why a 38% drawdown and a reaffirmed guide are both honest, and it means at the power layer you watch the contract-signing tape, not the capacity print. THE DECISIVE RESULT: E[FV] $86.9 vs $117.04 = -25.8% edge, and the reject is ROBUST TO THE HOUSE MACRO CALL - even at p(AI-BREAK)=0.05 the edge is -8.0%. The court was asked whether NRG is ownable on the pieces that do not depend on the AI narrative. It is - but not at this price, and that answer does not require the AI-BREAK call to be right. Path check adds the timing veto: this is day 0 of a new 52-week low on 8.6x volume in a 5-month crowded momentum unwind, with IV 52.4% vs HV 43.6%.

anti_masking_finding.finding: Planned, internal, orderly succession telegraphed 7 months before this print. Robert Gaudette (then EVP NRG Business and Wholesale Operations) became President immediately and CEO effective 2026-04-30 at the annual meeting. Coben's departure explicitly 'not the result of any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to the Company's operations, policies, or practices'; he stayed as adviser through end-FY2026. Antonio Carrillo (director since 2019) took the Chair, so governance was separated rather than concentrated. An abrupt CEO exit ahead of a guide-risk print would have been a serious mark; this is the opposite. Bull-side note: Gaudette came from the wholesale/business seat and is the architect of the large-load/BYOP strategy the stock just de-rated on.

print_correction: The first pass called the headline 'fine'. WRONG - this was an adjusted EPS MISS: $1.49 vs consensus ~$1.72-1.82 and $1.73 PY. Adjusted net income FELL $339M -> $315M while adj EBITDA rose $308M, because adjusted net interest went $136M -> $313M (2.3x) and D&A $344M -> $494M. THE LS POWER ACQUISITION IS EBITDA-ACCRETIVE AND EPS-DILUTIVE - combined with the 10.5% share issuance, that is the whole per-share story. Intraday sequencing is diagnostic: the stock traded UP to ~$142 pre-open on the release, then collapsed after the 9:00am ET call (open $140.00, high $140.03, low $112.50, close $117.04). The printed numbers were taken fine; the CALL broke it - on tracking-below-midpoint, $3.2B of self-funded BYOP capex, and the 3x leverage target slipping from 2028 to 2029.
street_check: Doctrine requires a sanity-check against the Street's LOWEST. Only one post-print action found: Scotiabank maintained Sector Outperform, PT cut $226 -> $211. No downgrades logged as of the evening of 08-04 (UNVERIFIED whether later actions exist). Recent PTs: Barclays $204, Wells Fargo $209, Scotiabank $211, BMO $212, UBS $216. Consensus PT $201.79. The original E[FV] of $86.9 sat 57% BELOW the Street's lowest - that check FAILED, and the reason was pricing a contracted IG-counterparty 15-year tolling asset and a 5.4 GW secured pipeline at zero. Bull and base cases raised accordingly. The remaining $95-vs-$202 gap IS the datacenter narrative, quantified - which is the deliverable the court was asked for.
